core_claim: We treat words like 'likely' and 'realistic possibility' as if they share a meaning, but 5,174 people show the same word can mean almost anything — and the disagreement lives between individuals, not within them.

edt_01.label: Hook — How likely is 'likely'?
edt_01.title: How likely is ‘likely’?
edt_01.editorial_notes: Open with the reader's own guess for 'realistic possibility'. 17.5%, 64%, 40-50% must be exact. Pair with the Kent 'serious possibility' 20-80% anecdote.

edt_02.label: The ladder that looks solid
edt_02.title: The ladder that looks solid
edt_02.editorial_notes: Present the mean ladder as deceptively reassuring; the chart should already hint at spread (box/range) to set up edt_03.

edt_03.label: Where consensus collapses
edt_03.title: Where consensus collapses
edt_03.editorial_notes: Disagreement (std/IQR) ranking is the spine of the piece. Realistic Possibility = most contested; extremes = tightest.

edt_04.label: The title fight — likely vs probable
edt_04.title: The title fight: likely vs probable
edt_04.editorial_notes: Keep both numbers visible: Likely wins on average (73 vs 71) but Probable wins head-to-head (78% vs 69%) — the method flips the winner.

edt_05.label: It's not you — it's us
edt_05.title: It’s not you, it’s us
edt_05.editorial_notes: 96.6% self-consistency is pivotal — proves variance is between people, not within. Must stay visible.

edt_06.label: The shortcuts in our heads
edt_06.title: The shortcuts in our heads
edt_06.editorial_notes: 53.6% multiples of 10, 31.2% ending in 5 must be exact. Last-digit spike chart. Sonification of the spiky last-digit distribution fits here.

edt_07.label: The explanations that don't explain
edt_07.title: The explanations that don’t explain
edt_07.editorial_notes: ALWAYS frame demographic effects as small (spread < 3pp). Keep sample-size caveat visible for Under-18/Norway outliers.

edt_08.label: Close — say the number
edt_08.title: Say the number
edt_08.editorial_notes: End on the practical lesson and reconnect to the reader's opening guess. End on a question, not a summary.
